ev.q: CDC analyzed results from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) for 1999--2006.
In 1999--2006, 20.3% of youths aged 12--19 years had abnormal lipids.
Among all youths, 20.3% had at least one abnormal lipid level
In 1999--2006, 20.3% of youths aged 12--19 years had abnormal lipids.
Compared with youths who were normal weight, overweight and obese youths were significantly more likely to have at least one abnormal lipid level
NHANES is a continuous cross-sectional survey of the health and nutritional status

methods_quotes.q: Significant differences in the prevalence of abnormal lipids as a function of demographic factors and overweight or obesity status were assessed using chi-square tests.
Prevalence ratios (PRs) were used to estimate relative risk for abnormal lipids levels.
The results from the fasting subsample are weighted to account for the probability of selection and nonresponse.
